title: Extradited From Brazil, Smuggler Pleads Guilty in Laredo Federal Court
excerpt: Saiful Islam, 39, pleaded guilty to federal smuggling charges after being extradited from Brazil; he faces at least three years in prison at sentencing in February 2027.
content:
A Bangladeshi man extradited from Brazil has pleaded guilty in federal court in the Southern District of Texas to running part of an international smuggling operation that moved migrants through South America, Central America and Mexico toward the United States.

Saiful Islam, 39, pleaded guilty on November 9 to one count of conspiracy to bring a person into the United States and two counts of bringing a person into the country for commercial advantage and private financial gain, according to the U.S. Department of Justice. The Laredo Morning Times reported the plea on November 15.

According to court documents cited by the Justice Department, Islam was part of a wide-ranging smuggling organization that facilitated travel for migrants from and through Brazil, across South America and Central America, and through Mexico so they could enter the United States illegally. Some migrants were transported along the Colombian coast in dangerous boats operated by intoxicated pilots, the department said, and others trekked through the Darién Gap, the jungle corridor between Colombia and Panama. Some were given documents belonging to other people, and at the border, migrants were told to wade across the Rio Grande or jump a fence.

Islam was extradited from Brazil to the United States in April 2026. An indictment filed April 13 in the Southern District of Texas alleged he facilitated migrants’ journeys from São Paulo and other locations, and his initial appearance was scheduled in Laredo before U.S. Magistrate Judge Christopher dos Santos.

As part of the plea, Islam agreed to forfeit money he collected from smuggled migrants. He is scheduled to be sentenced on February 17, 2027, and faces a mandatory minimum of three years in federal prison. A federal district judge will determine the final sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

The investigation was led by Homeland Security Investigations’ Phoenix office, with assistance from HSI offices in Laredo, Brasilia and Bogota, CBP’s Counter Network Division, the Brazilian Federal Police, the Colombian National Police, the U.S. Marshals Service and INTERPOL, under the Justice Department’s Joint Task Force Alpha initiative targeting human smuggling networks.

Sources:

  • U.S. Department of Justice, November 9, 2026
  • Laredo Morning Times, November 15, 2026
